newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank sells dollars after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank sells dollars after rate cut.

text.p: * Central Bank sells $16 million to stem peso fall-traders
The Philippine Central Bank moved to stop the peso's fall at midsession by selling dollars at 26.235 pesos, traders said.
The peso fell to a low of 26.235 pesos hours after the Central Bank cut its overnight borrowing and lending rates by 1.50 percentage points each to 11 and 13 percent respectively.
"The Central Bank's cut was too steep. That's why the peso is again weakening," said a foreign bank trader.
Last Monday, the peso closed at a low of 26.265 to the dollar from the previous close of 26.211.
That forced the Central Bank to raise its overnight rates on two straight days. But the Central Bank decided to ease its rates this Monday after the peso-dollar rate stabilised.
